# The paper's Figures 1-14, redrawn from our saved results

Generated by `python3 -B scripts/build_paper_figures.py` (PNG, SVG and PDF per figure). Every panel is drawn from saved counters, tables or run logs. Nothing is simulated while plotting and no paper graph is copied. Where the paper's plotted values exist as data they are drawn separately (hollow or grey) and labeled. Panels that need data we do not have are drawn as labeled empty panels instead of being left out.

How to read the labels: **public subset** means complete original public traces, not the paper's 1,559; **scaled** means a smaller synthetic workload than the paper's; **adaptation** means a different implementation or machine; **not run** or **not reproducible** means no data of ours is shown.

| Figure | File | What we drew | Evidence label | How it compares with the paper |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `fig01_mean_reduction` | Mean miss ratio reduction from FIFO, 7 algorithms, ours next to the paper's printed values; a third bar series averages every public trace we ran (19 at 10%) for the four algorithms run on all of them | public subset (7 traces with all policies; 19 traces for ARC, LRU, CLOCK, SIEVE) | Same ranking for SIEVE > ARC > LIRS > CACHEUS; LHD and CLOCK swap places; our means are about 2.2x smaller (7 traces versus 1,559, 82% proprietary) |
| 2 | `fig02_illustration` | FIFO-Reinsertion/CLOCK versus SIEVE on the same requests | illustration from the reference models | Shows the same difference as the paper: survivors move to the head under CLOCK and stay in place under SIEVE |
| 3 | `fig03_boxplots` (+ companions `fig03b_...`, `fig03c_...`) | Panels c and f (Twitter), all 11 algorithms, on the 5 (10%) and 7 (0.1%) Twitter traces that have them, each trace drawn as a dot; a, b, d, e labeled unavailable. The companion shows 4 algorithms on all 12 and 16 traces we ran | public subset (5 and 7 of 54 Twitter traces) | Several means are close to the paper's read-off ones at the large cache (SIEVE 0.10 vs 0.155, LHD 0.13 vs 0.16, LRU 0.09 vs 0.13) and lower at the small cache (SIEVE about 0 versus 0.08); the percentiles of 5-7 traces are rough. Companion `fig03c` adds the independent SIEVEREPRODUCTION snapshot (clusters 1-24, scaled copies) and the union: rank correlation of the means with the paper 0.96 / 0.98 (theirs), 0.99 / 0.98 (union of 44 / 45 clusters including 17 sampled clusters run here) |
| 4 | `fig04_public_scatter` (+ companions `fig04c_...`, `fig04d_...`) | Per-trace reduction for Meta CDN, Meta KV and Wiki next to the paper's points | public subset | Meta CDN and Wiki points sit on the paper's for most algorithms; TinyLFU uses the snapshot version, which differs from the paper's. Companion `fig04c` draws all 13 public traces x 11 algorithms from the imported snapshot (Tencent Photo on a 10% sample): 26 of 26 SIEVE points within 0.0001 of a paper dot; our own runs agree with theirs to 0.0001 on deterministic policies. The main figure's Tencent panel now carries our own runs (10% sample as markers, full size as stars; SIEVE within 0.0002 of both paper dots). Companion `fig04d` plots sample against full-size reductions (median gap about 0.0002; Hyperbolic and CACHEUS move more) |
| 5 | `fig05_best_algorithm_share` (+ companions `fig05b_...`, `fig05c_...`, `fig05d_...`, `fig05e_...`) | Winner shares per dataset over every public trace we ran (Meta CDN 3, Wiki 1, Meta KV 3, Twitter 16/12) among the same five contenders (SIEVE, ARC, CLOCK, LRU, LFU), with the paper's SIEVE share marked. The companion uses the paper's 11 candidates on 7 traces | public subset (23 traces at the small cache, 19 at the large) | Candidate set is smaller than the paper's, so shares are not directly comparable. Meta CDN: SIEVE wins 1 of 3 at the large cache, as in the paper (33%). Meta KV: SIEVE wins all 3 at both sizes among these contenders (paper: 100% large, 0% small). Twitter: SIEVE wins 42% (large) and 19% (small) of traces versus the paper's 30% and 11%. Tencent Photo is not in the main panel (no LFU) but was run with 11 candidates (sample and full size; `fig05d` counts the sample runs): SIEVE wins 0.5 at the large cache where the paper shows 1.0. Companion `fig05e` shows CACHEUS over nine seeds on the large cache: no spread (0.1150 on all), so the flip is not a seed draw. Companion `fig05c` shows the snapshot's bars against the paper's: 7 of 8 public-dataset bars equal, Tencent large differs (1/2 vs 1) |
| 6 | `fig06_throughput_adaptation` | Throughput versus threads for five designs | adaptation (own harness, 4-core laptop, not CacheLib) | Same direction (SIEVE scales best and its lead over LRU grows with threads); absolute numbers and 16 threads not comparable |
| 7 | `fig07_sifting_and_time` | State fixture and cumulative miss ratio over trace days for our traces | fixture plus public traces | Does not reproduce the paper's claim that SIEVE's advantage grows over time: on meta_reag ARC stays below SIEVE |
| 8 | `fig08_zipf_size` (+ companion `fig08c_...`) | Miss ratio and popular-object ratio versus cache size, alpha 1 | scaled study at the paper's apparent size: 10,000 objects, 10M requests, 3 seeds | **Miss ratios reproduced**: all 24 ARC/LRU/SIEVE points within 0.0008 of the paper's; popular ratio within 0.02 on average (0.09 at the smallest cache). The workload size was the missing piece; companion `fig08c` shows our earlier 1M-object curves beside it |
| 9 | `fig09_zipf_skew_and_hand` | Miss ratio and popular ratio versus skewness, hand position over time | scaled study: 10,000 objects (a, b) and a transplanted 1M-object setup (c) | Miss ratios within 0.002 of the paper at all 32 points and SIEVE lowest at every skew; popular ratio within 0.03; hand wraps 0 / 1-2 / 5-7 versus the paper's 0 / 2 / 7 (setup chosen by search against the paper, so reproducibility rather than prediction) |
| 10 | `fig10_workload_change` (+ companion `fig10c_...`) | Interval miss ratio and popular ratio across a workload change | original-scale local study | Same qualitative behavior: LFU never recovers, SIEVE spikes then recovers, LRU is unaffected. Companion `fig10c` repeats it at the 10,000-object support of Figure 8 (3,000-object cache, the one fitted choice): same order, LFU never recovers, SIEVE dips to 0.70 after the switch as in the paper; plateaus within 0.02, SIEVE's miss-ratio bump larger (0.24 vs about 0.18) |
| 11 | `fig11_instructions` | Instructions per request for LRU, FIFO, SIEVE with miss ratios | local matched study | Our miss ratios equal the paper's printed ones for alpha 0.8 at the large cache (0.51/0.55/0.43); SIEVE needs the fewest instructions except alpha 1.2 at the large cache, the paper's stated exception |
| 12 | `fig12_advanced_algorithms` | Original versus LRU-replaced-by-SIEVE for 4 algorithms; Belady variants on one trace | public subset (7 traces, every point shown) | Does not reproduce the paper's average gain: here replacing LRU with SIEVE lowers the mean for ARC and LeCaR; seven traces cannot settle this |
| 13 | `fig13_byte_miss_ratio` | Byte miss ratio reduction on 3 Meta CDN traces | public subset | SIEVE gives a small positive byte reduction at both sizes; the paper's box statistics over 1,492 CDN traces are not reproducible |
| 14 | `fig14_lrb_wiki_bytes` | Two labeled empty panels | not run | LRB and its Wiki2018/Wiki2019 traces were not available |

Source tables are named in each figure's footnote and in the [figure catalog](../../docs/FIGURE_CATALOG.md). The coverage matrix (`docs/coverage_matrix.csv`) gives the status of every panel.
